titleZh: SpaceX在星舰基地的星舰进展更新
summaryEn: Musk's Starbase all-hands Starship progress update covering flight tests and next-generation vehicle plans.
summaryZh: 马斯克在星舰基地面向全体员工所作的星舰进展更新，涵盖飞行测试和下一代飞行器计划。

segments.textEn: All right. It's been an incredible year. The SpaceX team I think is the best space team that has ever been assembled on the face of the earth by far. And the achievements of the past year demonstrate that I think to a degree that is mind blowing. Like what you have achieved over the past year is nothing short of incredible. And one day we will indeed occupy Mars.
segments.textZh: 好了。这是不可思议的一年。我认为，SpaceX团队是迄今为止地球上组建过的最优秀的太空团队。而过去一年的成就证明了这一点，我认为其程度令人震撼。你们过去一年所取得的成就简直不可思议。终有一天，我们确实会进驻火星。

segments.textEn: So let's go through everything that SpaceX has achieved that you've done and it's actually going to take a while by the way. This is going to take a minute.
segments.textZh: 那么，让我们逐项回顾SpaceX所取得的、由你们完成的一切，顺便说一下，这实际上会花上一些时间。这得花一会儿。

segments.textEn: So first of all, with Belkin we have achieved the most launches of any rocket in a single year ever. So the next best was the Soviet Soyuz, which I think did a little over 60 launches in a year and we did 96.
segments.textZh: 那么首先，凭借贝尔金，我们实现了有史以来任何火箭在单个年份中的最多发射次数。所以下一个最好的成绩是苏联的联盟号，我记得它一年进行了略多于60次发射，而我们进行了96次。

segments.textEn: So.
segments.textZh: 所以。

segments.textEn: This, this, yeah. So no other family of orbital class rockets has launched more than 63 times a year. That was Soyuz and we did 50% more. Falcon Heavy also surpassed in terms of heavy lift vehicles the record for Saturn V, which I think that yeah, we, with five launches last year we exceeded the Saturn V record. So that was like pretty incredible. And Falcon Heavy. So this gives you a sense in pictures of how incredible that was.
segments.textZh: 这，这，是的。所以，没有其他轨道级火箭家族一年发射超过63次。那个纪录属于联盟号，而我们多了50%。就重型运载火箭而言，猎鹰重型也超过了土星5号的纪录，我想，是的，我们凭借去年5次发射，超过了土星5号的纪录。所以这真是相当不可思议。还有猎鹰重型。所以这些图片能让你直观感受到那有多么不可思议。

segments.textEn: You know, for a while there I was like, when I was like, I'd be posting something, is this like the launch that just happened or the one that is happening or like because there were like three launches that happened in the space of a few days. So but this is all the launches on one page and yeah, so it's really, really incredible. All made it to orbit, all landed. So just a huge hand for the Falcon team. That was incredible.
segments.textZh: 你知道，有一阵子我会想，当我发些什么东西时，这说的是刚刚发生的那次发射，还是正在进行的那次，或者是，因为短短几天里就进行了大概3次发射。所以，不过这一页上是所有的发射，是的，所以真的、真的不可思议。全都进入了轨道，全都着陆了。所以，请为猎鹰团队热烈鼓掌。那太不可思议了。

segments.textEn: So, And two thirds of the missions were Starlink, but a third were for other customers, for NASA, for other communication satellites. So it was a combination of our of Starlink plus a lot of other missions. So even if you just take the non Starlink portion of the flights, that was more than any other vehicle. Last year by a long shot. We launched NASA's Psyche, ESA's Euclid, the X37B space plane, multiple transporter missions, we launched missions for OneWeb, ViaSat, and we're actually on contract to launch Amazon's Kuiper Constellation.
segments.textZh: 所以，其中2/3的任务是星链任务，但1/3是为其他客户执行的，包括NASA和其他通信卫星。所以，这是我们的星链任务加上许多其他任务的组合。因此，即使只看飞行任务中非星链的部分，也远远多于去年的任何其他飞行器。我们发射了NASA的灵神星探测器、欧洲航天局的欧几里得空间望远镜、X37B空天飞机以及多次Transporter任务；我们还为OneWeb、ViaSat发射了任务，而且我们实际上已经签约，将发射亚马逊的柯伊伯星座。

segments.textEn: And we treat everyone fairly. So you know, just one. And we managed to do 19 flights on a single Falcon 9 booster, which is really incredible in three and a half years. So and that vehicle did that booster, did 860 satellites and delivered 260 metric tons to orbit. So it's like wow. So there's a lot of wows.
segments.textZh: 而且我们公平对待所有人。所以，你知道，就一个。而且我们成功让同一枚猎鹰9号助推器执行了19次飞行，在3年半的时间里，这真的不可思议。所以，那枚飞行器确实，那枚助推器，发射了860颗卫星，并将260公吨送入轨道。所以，简直是，哇。所以有很多个“哇”。

segments.textEn: And it's worth, you know, like how long ago was it that we landed a booster? It was actually eight years ago in December, roughly eight years ago. And since that time we've landed 260 times. So 260 landings, just like wow.
segments.textZh: 而且值得一提的是，你知道，我们让助推器着陆是多久以前？实际上是8年前的12月，大约8年前。从那以后，我们已经着陆了260次。所以是260次着陆，简直让人惊叹。

segments.textEn: I mean there were a lot of people that said that it couldn't be done. And then there were a lot of people that said even if it could be done, it's gonna, it's a dumb idea that, no, that it wouldn't, it wouldn't pay off, that it wouldn't, you know, wouldn't make sense. But we've shown that in fact it is absolutely the right idea. Reusability is the key to a great future in space. It's essential. We need reusability for truck, it's just like we have reusability for cars, for airplanes, for bicycles, for horses.
segments.textZh: 我是说，当时有很多人说这是做不到的。然后也有很多人说，即使能做到，这也会，这也是个愚蠢的想法，说不，它不会有回报，它不会，你知道，不会有意义。但我们已经证明，事实上这绝对是正确的想法。可重复使用是通往伟大太空未来的关键。它至关重要。我们需要卡车能够重复使用，就像汽车、飞机、自行车和马匹都能重复使用一样。

segments.textEn: Obviously reusability is essential. And the fundamental invention that is necessary for humanity to become a multi planet species is, is a full and rapidly, basically rapidly reusable reliable rockets.
segments.textZh: 显然，可重复使用至关重要。而要让人类成为多行星物种，所必需的根本性发明是，是完全且快速地，基本上是可快速重复使用的可靠火箭。

segments.textEn: So like space pirate.
segments.textZh: 所以，就像太空海盗。

segments.textEn: So it's, I mean it's incredible how much has happened in eight years. So you know, I wonder what will things be like eight years from now?
segments.textZh: 所以，我是说，8年间发生了这么多事情，真是不可思议。所以，你知道，我很好奇8年后会是什么样子？

segments.textEn: Now hopefully we have, I think we will have landed on Mars and I think we will have sent people to the moon and maybe if we get lucky, we will have sent people to Mars within eight years.
segments.textZh: 现在，希望我们已经，我想我们届时已经登陆火星，我想我们会把人送上月球；而且如果运气好的话，我们会在8年内把人送上火星。

segments.textEn: You know the, you know the key question sort of, I think about for civilization is the key test perhaps for civilization is do we make it through the spermy great filter of going from a one planet civilization to a multi planet civilization?
segments.textZh: 你知道，那个，你知道，我对文明思考的某种关键问题是，对文明的关键考验或许是：我们能否通过那个精子般的、从单行星文明迈向多行星文明的“大过滤器”？

segments.textEn: And if we do become a multi planet civilization, we may go out there to other star systems and discover many long dead one planet civilizations. And we don't want to be one of them. That's lame. We don't want to blame one planet civilizations, but I think we should always regard civilization as fragile, as not something that, not a situation where there is an inevitable upward trajectory. I mean I read a lot about history and if you look at, if you read history, you see that civilizations are anything but permanent.
segments.textZh: 而如果我们真的成为多行星文明，我们也许会走向其他恒星系统，并发现许多早已消亡的单行星文明。我们不想成为其中之一。那太逊了。我们并不是要责怪单行星文明，但我认为我们应该始终把文明视为脆弱的，而不是某种，不是一个必然会沿着上升轨迹发展的局面。我读过很多历史，而如果你审视，如果你阅读历史，就会看到文明绝非永恒。

segments.textEn: That many civilizations have risen and fallen over the years, over the centuries and millennia, and.
segments.textZh: 许多文明在这些年里、在数百年和数千年间兴起又衰落，而且。

segments.textEn: Eventually the sun will expand, boil the oceans and destroy all life on earth. Now admittedly that's you know, several hundred million years in the future, but it's only about maybe 10 or 20% of the existence of Earth itself. If Earth is four and a half billion years old, then another 10, 10, 20% longer and life wouldn't, or intelligent life would not have evolved because it's taken us a long time to get to this point.
segments.textZh: 太阳最终会膨胀，煮沸海洋并摧毁地球上的所有生命。诚然，那是，你知道，未来几亿年后的事，但那大约只相当于地球自身存在时间的10%或20%。如果地球已有45亿年历史，那么再延长10%、10%、20%，生命就不会，或者说智慧生命就不会进化出来，因为我们花了很长时间才走到这一步。

segments.textEn: So that's really the key test. Do we become a self sustaining, multi planet civilization.
segments.textZh: 所以，那才是真正的关键考验。我们是否会成为一个能够自给自足的多行星文明。

segments.textEn: While civilization still exists, or don't we? I think that's really the key question.
segments.textZh: 趁文明仍然存在时做到这一点，还是做不到？我认为这才是真正的关键问题。

segments.textEn: I think we've got a good chance, but it's not a sure thing.
segments.textZh: 我认为我们成功的机会很大，但这并非板上钉钉。

segments.textEn: That's why time is of the essence. I think we want to make Mars self sustaining as quickly as possible. It's not just a question of getting people to Mars, but it's getting enough tonnage and equipment to Mars to make, enable Mars to be self sustaining. The key test being that if the resupply ships from Earth stop coming for any reason, do we, does Mars die out or does it continue? That's the, that's the really the fundamental threshold to pass the, the Fermi paradox.
segments.textZh: 所以时间至关重要。我认为我们要尽快让火星实现自给自足。问题不只是把人送上火星，而是要把足够吨位的物资和设备送上火星，从而让，使火星能够自给自足。关键考验是，如果来自地球的补给飞船因任何原因停止抵达，我们，火星是会灭亡，还是会延续下去？那就是，那才是真正需要跨过的基本门槛，费米悖论。

segments.textEn: Great Filter. The Fermi paradox is where are the aliens? You know, if life is common, if intelligent life is common, shouldn't we see a lot of evidence of it? Now I get asked a lot about, you know, aliens actually, and I usually say I am one. Well, actually I used to be, according to, you know, Homeland Security, it said alien registration card. Literally. I was like, okay, so.
segments.textZh: 大过滤器。费米悖论就是：外星人在哪里？你知道，如果生命很普遍，如果智慧生命很普遍，我们难道不应该看到大量相关证据吗？其实很多人会问我，你知道，关于外星人的事，而我通常会说我就是一个。嗯，实际上我以前是，根据，你知道，美国国土安全部的说法，那张卡上写着“外侨登记卡”。确实如此。我当时就想，好吧，所以。

segments.textEn: But the truth is I actually have not seen any evidence of aliens, which I think is maybe a bit more troubling than if I had.
segments.textZh: 但事实是，我确实没有见过任何外星人的证据，而我认为这或许比我见过证据更令人不安。

segments.textEn: I have not seen any and I'd be on it and I can pretty much guarantee that I would post about it instantly. Okay.
segments.textZh: 我一个都没见过，而且我会关注这件事，我几乎可以保证，我会立刻发帖谈论它。好吧。

segments.textEn: I was like, yep, we got one.
segments.textZh: 我当时就说，对，我们发现了一个。

segments.textEn: This is a spaceship for sure. But I have not seen anything. So that leads me to think that we're more likely to be a tiny candle of consciousness in a vast emptiness, a vast darkness. You know, that the civilization that we have is really just this very, very small candle in a vast darkness. And we just must do everything possible to ensure that that candle does not go out.
segments.textZh: 这肯定是一艘宇宙飞船。但我什么都没见过。所以这让我认为，我们更有可能只是浩瀚虚空、无边黑暗中的一支微小意识烛火。你知道，我们拥有的文明其实只是浩瀚黑暗中这支非常、非常微小的烛火。我们必须尽一切可能确保这支烛火不会熄灭。

segments.textEn: Yeah, anyway, I think we can do it. So, you know, but we need to move fast because you just never know. I mean there could be, you know, at any given point there's a, like Stephen Hawking actually, I believe, said that he thought there was like roughly a 1% chance in any given century of civilization ending. That was his rough estimate. I think it actually might be higher than that. So we just want to go there fast.
segments.textZh: 是的，总之，我认为我们能做到。所以，你知道，但我们必须迅速行动，因为你永远不知道。我是说，可能会有，你知道，在任何时候都有一个，像史蒂芬·霍金实际上，我相信，曾说过，他认为文明在任何一个世纪终结的概率大约是1%。那是他的粗略估计。我认为实际概率甚至可能比这更高。所以我们只想尽快到达那里。

segments.textEn: So this is the getting Back to Falcon 9 back to reality.
segments.textZh: 所以这是，回到 Falcon 9，回到现实。

segments.textEn: This is, these are all the launches we've done. And you can see how the cadence of launches has rapidly increased over time.
segments.textZh: 这是，这些是我们完成的所有发射。你们可以看到，随着时间推移，发射节奏是如何迅速加快的。

segments.textEn: I think people online have actually assembled videos showing every launch and it just gets like crazy fast as you get to 2023.
segments.textZh: 我想网上其实有人制作了展示每次发射的视频，而当视频推进到2023年时，速度就快得近乎疯狂。

segments.textEn: So yeah, so we've, and we've done a 19, 3 flight. We're now qualifying Falcon 9 to be able to do 40 flights and we're aiming for maybe as much as 150 flights this year. So. And then let's not forget fairing recovery, because actually a lot of people don't realize we recover the fairing as well. This was actually very difficult to recover the fairing, so that's an immense amount of effort. But we now quite regularly recover the fairing and we've reflown fairings 300 times.
segments.textZh: 所以，是的，所以我们已经，而且我们已经完成了一次19、3飞行。我们现在正对 Falcon 9 进行资质认证，使其能够完成40次飞行，而我们今年的目标可能高达150次飞行。所以。还有，别忘了整流罩回收，因为实际上很多人没有意识到，我们也会回收整流罩。回收整流罩其实非常困难，所以这投入了极其巨大的努力。但我们现在已经能够相当常规地回收整流罩，而且整流罩已经复飞了300次。

segments.textEn: So congrats to the fairing recovery team. That was actually pretty damn hard.
segments.textZh: 所以祝贺整流罩回收团队。那实际上真他妈难。

segments.textEn: Oh, and then of course we do operate basically a small navy. I think people don't always know that, but we have, you know, drone ships and support ships of various kinds. So we've got a small fleet of ships and we operate them very efficiently.
segments.textZh: 哦，当然，我们基本上还运营着一支小型舰队。我觉得人们并不总是知道这一点，不过我们有，你知道，无人船以及各种类型的支援船。所以我们有一支小型船队，而且运营得非常高效。

segments.textEn: People also sometimes don't know the size. Like you can see the size of the ship by the person walking around on it. It's not small, so it looks cool. I like this sort of kind of a Darth Vader aesthetic, but it's. I like it.
segments.textZh: 人们有时也不知道它有多大。比如，你可以通过在船上走动的人看出船的大小。它并不小，所以看起来很酷。我喜欢这种有点达斯·维德式的美学，不过它。反正我喜欢。

segments.textEn: So. And, and we're also getting much better with the pad turnaround. We achieved a three day pad turnaround and I think we're aiming to hopefully, I think, get under 24 hours pad turnaround by the end of this year.
segments.textZh: 所以。而且，而且我们在发射台周转方面也做得越来越好了。我们实现了3天的发射台周转，我想我们的目标是，希望，我觉得，在今年年底前把发射台周转时间缩短到24小时以内。

segments.textEn: So in terms of. Yeah. Launch rate.
segments.textZh: 所以就……而言。是的。发射频率。

segments.textEn: Yeah. So it's been 15 years since Flight 1 of Falcon 1. I'm sorry, Flight 4 of Falcon 1, the first one to reach orbit.
segments.textZh: 对。所以自猎鹰1号第1次飞行以来已经有15年了。抱歉，是猎鹰1号第4次飞行，也就是第一次进入轨道的那次。

segments.textEn: So 15 years since we've got anything at all to orbit.
segments.textZh: 所以，距离我们首次把任何东西送入轨道已经过去15年了。

segments.textEn: Yeah. And now we're aiming to have 150 flights or thereabouts this year. So.
segments.textZh: 对。而现在我们的目标是今年完成150次左右的飞行。所以。

segments.textEn: And these are big rockets at this point. Falcon 1 is a little rocket. In fact, when I see Falcon 1 right now, I was like, man, I think I'd probably tuck that under my arm, just take it home with me, you know, it was like launch it in the backyard or something. It looks so cute.
segments.textZh: 而且现在这些都是大型火箭。猎鹰1号是一枚小火箭。事实上，现在看到猎鹰1号时，我就会想，天啊，我觉得自己大概能把它夹在胳膊下面，直接带回家，你知道，就像在后院发射它之类的。它看起来太可爱了。

segments.textEn: But at the time, Falcon 1 did seem like extremely, it was extremely difficult. It took us four flights to reach orbit and it did seem kind of big at the time, but now it's like adorable thing.
segments.textZh: 但在当时，猎鹰1号确实显得极其，它极其困难。我们用了4次飞行才进入轨道，而且当时它看起来确实有点大，但现在它就像个可爱的小东西。

segments.textEn: So. Yeah.
segments.textZh: 所以。对。

segments.textEn: So I think the most profound metric or the metric that really describes the magnitude of what SpaceX achieved in 2023 is the master orbit number. So. And you can See that, the incredible change just year over year. So 2021, we're slightly below rest of world 22 we I think roughly doubled what the rest of the world did. And last year we were 80% of all master orbit. So when rest of the world we mean like the rest of US industry, you know, Europe, India, China, Japan, everyone.
segments.textZh: 所以我认为，最深刻的指标，或者说真正体现SpaceX在2023年所取得成就之规模的指标，是入轨质量。所以。你可以看到，仅仅逐年相比就发生了不可思议的变化。所以2021年，我们略低于世界其他地区，22年，我认为我们大约是世界其他地区的2倍。而去年，我们占全部入轨质量的80%。所以我们所说的世界其他地区，是指美国其他同行，你知道，还有欧洲、印度、中国、日本，所有人。

segments.textEn: So there's not a lot of industries where a company is doing like 80% of everything.
segments.textZh: 所以，没有多少行业会由一家公司完成全部工作中的大约80%。

segments.textEn: And then what's really mind boggling is that number should increase by 50% this year. So I guess on the order of like 90% of all mass to orbit, not counting starship. So if we start, as we start launching starship, Starship is like roughly 100 tons to orbit. With every flight there's a path to getting starship to do over 200 tons with full reusability to 200 tons to useful orbit with full reusability.
segments.textZh: 然后真正令人难以置信的是，这个数字今年应该还会增长50%。所以我估计，大约会占全部入轨质量的90%，这还不算星舰。所以如果我们开始，当我们开始发射星舰时，星舰每次飞行大约能把100吨送入轨道。有一条路径可以让星舰在完全可重复使用的情况下做到超过200吨，在完全可重复使用的情况下把200吨送入实用轨道。

segments.textEn: And yeah, it's really an incredible amount. 1200 tons of useful load to orbit last year.
segments.textZh: 而且，对，这确实是一个不可思议的数量。去年送入轨道的有效载荷达到1200吨。

segments.textEn: Yeah, that's just astounding. So I think that really deserves a round of applause. Wow. I mean that's the most mind blowing.
segments.textZh: 对，这简直令人震惊。所以我认为这确实值得一轮掌声。哇。我的意思是，这最令人难以置信。

segments.textEn: And the rate of increase is just astonishing. Now these numbers will actually look very small in the future. In order to build a city on Mars, we'll need to be kind of in the million ton to orbit range.
segments.textZh: 而且增长速度简直惊人。未来这些数字实际上会显得非常小。为了在火星上建造一座城市，我们需要达到大约100万吨入轨质量的水平。

segments.textEn: So maybe a little higher, ideally a little higher.
